topics.topic: Input representation and lexical preservation required by canonical_bytes
questions: What representation must `canonical_bytes` receive so it can distinguish integer, decimal and exponent spellings and apply the new lexical number refusal after JSON parsing would otherwise erase that distinction?
What representation must canonical_bytes receive so it can distinguish the newly refused integer spelling from other spellings that decode to the same runtime number?
Does `canonical_bytes` receive the original JSON text or an already-parsed value, and which operation preserves enough lexical information to enforce depth and the new number-spelling refusal?

judgement.why: P1 judged the same canonicalization input-representation, lexical-number, and depth-enforcement question on unchanged deciding text.

precedent.topic: Canonicalization input domain, lexical-number acceptance, and depth-limit enforcement
quotes: canonical_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] MUST parse json_text as one JSON value and emit its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form encoded as UTF-8: object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names, numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (an integral double without a fraction or exponent, so a number written 1.0 becomes 1), strings escaped exactly as JCS prescribes, and no whitespace; it applies no Unicode normalization, so two texts that differ only in normalization give different bytes.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1) and is neither held exactly by an IEEE double nor written exactly as that double's ECMAScript shortest round-trip form — 100000000000000000000, which a double holds exactly, and 18014398509481990, the form JCS writes for 1.801439850948199e+16, are each that double, so canonical bytes always parse again to the same bytes —, when the value nests deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, the depth of a scalar being 0 and of an array or object one more than its deepest element or member value, a member's name adding no level, 1 when it has none, found while parsing and never by a recursion deeper than that constant, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.

content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For every content variant of IdentitySubject (contract_version, implementation, trial_case, flow_version, stored_value, corpus) MUST build one JSON object whose members are exactly the variant's fields keyed by field name, subject_kind included, with nested models as objects keyed by field name, tuples as arrays, enum members as their value text, None as null and JSON-text fields such as value_schema kept as JSON strings, take its canonical bytes with canonical_bytes and return the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of those bytes.

content_identity: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST let NonCanonicalValueError from canonical_bytes propagate unchanged when any JSON text the subject carries cannot be represented canonically; it computes no partial identity.
precedent.why: The later notes define the text input, complete rejection domain, lexical-number rule, depth enforcement, wrapper canonicalization and propagated error.

topics.topic: Reporting and handling over-depth mapped lists in assemble_mapped_lists and plan_run
questions: What result must `assemble_mapped_lists` return for an over-depth mapped list, and must `plan_run` treat that result identically to an over-size list when deriving the node failure with no record?
What result must assemble_mapped_lists return for an over-depth mapped list, and how must plan_run distinguish or consume that result to fail the mapped node and derive the trace?
How does `assemble_mapped_lists` report an excessive-depth list to `run_graph`, and is that result distinguishable from excessive byte size?

judgement.why: P2 judged the same over-depth mapped-list reporting and run-planning propagation question on unchanged deciding text.

precedent.topic: Over-depth mapped-list result and its propagation through run planning
quotes: assemble_mapped_lists: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST measure every value list against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant before it answers anything, and when the canonical bytes of any exceed it, or canonical_bytes refuses the list with NonCanonicalValueError — which for a list of stored canonical values happens only when it nests deeper than the release depth ceiling —, answer ListsOverCeiling naming the node and the first such port in the order given, with no list; it is given only the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output, so every delivered list of a node is measured before any of them is written or delivered.

plan_run: [BEHAVIOR] A mapped node's elements are the positions of a non-empty list delivered to its map_over port, counted from the JSON array its StoredValue holds — read with read_value_bytes of a StoredValueSource naming its value_id, or the canonical_json of an AssembledValueList not yet written — or the files of its SpooledFilesRef; a list with no position gives no element, and a mapped node over an empty list is instead ready with over_empty_list and one element without map_index, which stands for the node and is no position of the list, whose sources are the node's inputs as delivered — its map_over port's source is the source of the empty list itself, a RecordedSource or a MappedListSource, never a ListElementSource, which exists only for an element with a map_index; a mapped node concludes only when every element concluded, succeeded only when all succeeded. For a succeeded mapped node with elements, the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output are asked of assemble_mapped_lists, an output no edge takes being asked nothing: ListsOverCeiling makes the node failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, with no record of its own and every element record staying as it is.
precedent.why: The later notes make assemble_mapped_lists convert either size excess or excessive depth into ListsOverCeiling and specify exactly how plan_run propagates it.

precedent.topic: Sandbox byte accounting and failure classification for outputs without canonical bytes
quotes: runner_source: [BEHAVIOR] When run returned, the program MUST write one returned message: whether the value is a dict with only str keys and, for each key, its form — json for a value port whose value json.dumps accepts with sort_keys=True, separators (',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False and allow_nan=False (for a many value port, a list), file for a file port whose value is bytes, file_list for a many file port whose value is a list of bytes, not_representable otherwise and for a key that is no output port. Before it builds that message it MUST pre-count the representable outputs against output_bytes — each value output as the UTF-8 bytes of that json.dumps, each file as its bytes — and when the pre-count exceeds output_bytes write a resource hit and no outputs; a MemoryError while it pre-counts, encodes or writes the outputs is a resource hit too, so an output too large to send concludes resource_exhausted rather than crashed. It writes nothing to standard output or standard error.

judge_execution: [BEHAVIOR] MUST decide from the observation, the output ports and the bounds it is given and the release constants it imports, nothing else, and run nothing. The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output — for an output whose JSON text canonical_bytes refuses, the UTF-8 bytes of that text as returned — and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated. A bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it — the report's resource_hit, the observation's channel_over_bound or that count over bounds.output_bytes; the parent kills an environment only for its wall deadline (owner, 2026-10-06) and for its channel bound, which execute_function observes as channel_over_bound.

judge_execution: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] When cleanup was confirmed the outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the report's resource_hit is true — the runner hit its memory, process or scratch limit, the scratch limit being the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SANDBOX_SCRATCH_BYTES_MAX constant, which runner_arguments writes as file_size_limit into the runner's command line and which is no field of ResourceBounds or RunnerLaunch —, the observation's channel_over_bound holds, or the output count exceeds bounds.output_bytes; sandbox_violation when the report holds any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the report says crashed, the runner exited abnormally, or no returned message was read — the report's returned is None: read_runner_report always gives a RunnerReport, for a channel that carried nothing one with no trap hit, no resource hit, crashed false, failure None and returned None, so the observation always holds a report; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value and spool ceilings are applied by the module that stores or spools an output.
precedent.why: The later notes define serialization, count only representable payload bytes rather than report framing, classify unserializable values as not_representable, and fix outcome precedence.
